newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WEST INDIES APOLOGISE FOR LARA OUTBURST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WEST INDIES APOLOGISE FOR LARA OUTBURST.

text.p: West Indies tour management have apologised for Brian Lara's behaviour after his angry confronation with Australia coach Geoff Marsh during the second test in Sydney, local media reported on Thursday.
The West Indies vice-captain was infuriated over his dismissal on the fifth and final day on Tuesday and took his complaint to the Australian dressing room.
"It's not a big thing and it's finished now. We have apologised to the Australians," West Indies tour manager Clive Lloyd told The Australian newspaper.
Lara made his outburst only minutes after he was caught by wicketkeeper Ian Healy in controversial circumstances at the Sydney Cricket Ground.
Healy tumbled forward to take the catch but television replays raised doubts as to whether the ball had carried into his gloves.
The dismissal proved a key turning point in the match, accelerating West Indies' capitulation in a 124-run defeat. Australia now lead the five-test series two-nil.
In his outburst, Lara, still wearing his pads, told Marsh that Healy would not be welcome in the West Indies dressing room, The Australian reported.

In full view of the rest of the team, Lloyd later strongly criticised Lara for his behaviour and for breaking a pledge made by both sides to improve relations, The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported, citing West Indies sources.
In their post-match interviews, both Healy and Australia captain Mark Taylor played down the incident, saying they had no doubt the catch was clean.
But West Indies captain Courtney Walsh refused to do likewise, saying: "Everyone saw it and I'd rather not comment".
The intense rivalry between Australia and West Indies has spilled over several times in the past.
Four years ago, Healy and Lara were involved in an unsavoury incident in a Brisbane test when the West Indies number three was stumped in questionable circumstances.
Television replays of that dismissal showed that Healy did not have the ball in his gloves when he removed the bails, a failing that should have meant Lara stayed at the crease.
Lara, the world record holder for the highest score in test and first-class cricket, has endured a miserable series so far, falling cheaply in both innings in the Sydney test.
Australia and West Indies will play each other in a limited overs match in Melbourne on Friday.
